title: Rule of Thirds and Asymmetric Balance
description: Positioning primary focal anchors along horizontal and vertical dividing thirds or their grid intersections, yielding natural visual dynamism and comfortable visual flow.

title: Central Geometric Symmetry
description: Direct central alignment with bilateral symmetry, creating a powerful, monumental, formal, and authoritative presence often seen in architectural photography and Stanley Kubrick cinema.

title: Leading Lines and S-Curves
description: Utilizing architectural corridors, roads, rivers, railings, or ridgelines as linear guides drawing the viewer's gaze from the foreground into the deep focal horizon.

title: Framing within a Frame (Sub-framing)
description: Framing the primary subject within natural or architectural apertures such as archways, windows, foliage, doorways, or shadow silhouettes to intensify contextual intimacy.

title: Dutch Angle and Dynamic Slanted Horizon
description: Intentionally canting the camera horizon by 15-45 degrees to invoke psychological tension, unease, disorientation, or kinetic momentum in dramatic narrative scenes.
